target.title: fix(models): retain generated models with richer input metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Generated provider catalog shards can advertise `audio` or `video` input metadata. The session `ModelRegistry` disk schema accepted only `text` and `image`, so a MiniMax or NVIDIA shard containing those known modalities failed validation and contributed no models. Configured primaries such as `minimax/MiniMax-M3` could then disappear from the registry and fall back unexpectedly.

Fixes #97048.

## Why This Change Was Made

The TypeBox schema in `src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts` validates agent `models.json` and generated plugin catalog files; it is not the public configuration schema. The public `ModelDefinitionConfig` type and Zod configuration schema already accept `text`, `image`, `audio`, and `video`, and model preparation can persist those values into `models.json`.

This change aligns that disk-ingress schema with the existing metadata contract, then projects the metadata at the `ModelRegistry.parseModels` boundary into the narrower `@openclaw/llm-core` execution contract, which remains `text`/`image` only. It deliberately does not widen `packages/llm-core`, provider transports, model-list output, or other runtime/public surfaces.

The regression uses two generated, plugin-owned shards matching the reported production rows:

- MiniMax `MiniMax-M3` with `video` metadata.
- NVIDIA `microsoft/phi-4-multimodal-instruct` with `audio` metadata.

Both rows must survive validation while their runtime `Model.input` values remain `['text', 'image']`. A non-empty row advertising only unsupported runtime modalities is omitted from the execution registry, while an explicit empty input list retains its existing `[]` meaning.

Thanks @ly-wang19 for the original fix and @zackchiutw for the detailed report.

## User Impact

Affected generated catalog rows remain available after refresh or restart, so configured primaries no longer disappear solely because the provider catalog includes richer media metadata. Existing LLM execution behavior is unchanged: transports still receive only the supported `text`/`image` runtime input contract, and unsupported-only models are not exposed as selectable runtime models.

## Evidence

- Published prep SHA: `317966f66751e5f3dccf39242bed5acdfefc3c71`, rebased on `b5ba0771f9abacb6f09e563a9d7f3a6b19476ab7`.
- Fresh Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kx3hzy5pjxnbgpzk137ybt48` ([Actions run 29022563114](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29022563114)) completed with wrapper `exitCode: 0`:
  - `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/model-registry.test.ts` — 9/9 tests.
  - `pnpm tsgo:core`.
  - `pnpm tsgo:core:test`.
  - Targeted Oxlint for the registry implementation and regression.
  - `pnpm check:changelog-attributions`.
- Local exact-final fallback `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/model-registry.test.ts` passed 9/9 tests.
- Brokered public-network AWS Crabbox focused run `run_69ddd4a8bece` passed 9/9 tests; full touched-surface run `run_6a7283abde04` passed the same focused suite, both typecheck lanes, targeted Oxlint, and changelog attribution.
- Live production-loader probe `run_9cd01e7b3f4c` loaded both generated shards with `error: null` and returned both affected models with runtime inputs `['text', 'image']`.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no findings; patch correct at 0.98 confidence.
- `git diff --check` passed; published branch diff is 3 files, +92/-3.

The initial Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kx3f2z24xvhmmchyx9700245` remained capacity-queued for 4m35s and never acquired a runner, so the public-network AWS fallback supplied the first proof while a fresh replacement Testbox was acquired. The replacement Testbox completed the final patch-tree gate and was stopped after success. The subsequent rebase incorporated unrelated `main` changes plus adjacent changelog entries without changing this patch's three-file diff.

All tests and the production-loader probe used synthetic in-memory API-key values, contacted no provider endpoint, and required no live provider credentials.
